title: Mật độ đô thị · Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some societies are considering encouraging high-density housing around public transport stations. What problems could this create, and what measures could be taken to address them?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

grammar.why: Trong câu “Housing near stations links decisions about urban growth to the number of people who can use public transport conveniently.”, cụm “can” đặt hệ quả ở mức khả năng thay vì khẳng định chắc chắn. Nhiều cư dân trong khoảng đi bộ tạo cầu đều cho vận tải công cộng và giảm nhu cầu xe thứ hai. Cơ chế là vị trí và mật độ kết hợp, không phải nhà cao tầng tự giảm phát thải.

grammar.name: Đối chiếu hoặc đồng thời với while
grammar.example: If these are not expanded, shorter travel can come with overcrowded facilities, while rising land values may exclude the lower-income households expected to benefit most from convenient transport.
grammar.why: Trong câu “If these are not expanded, shorter travel can come with overcrowded facilities, while rising land values may exclude the lower-income households expected to benefit most from convenient transport.”, while nối hai diễn biến hoặc yêu cầu cần xét cùng nhau; ở đây phải giữ cả hai phía để không biến điều kiện giới hạn thành phủ nhận toàn bộ lợi ích. Không suy ra mọi khu dày đều đáng sống hoặc giá phải chăng. Nếu hộ thu nhập thấp bị đẩy xa ga, lợi ích vị trí rơi vào người vốn có nhiều lựa chọn.

paragraphs: Housing near stations links decisions about urban growth to the number of people who can use public transport conveniently. Concentrated development can overload facilities and exclude poorer households, so housing growth must be coordinated with schools, public space and affordability.

Density without adequate schools and open space can reduce everyday liveability. Concentrating homes also concentrates demand for schools, public space and local services. If these are not expanded, shorter travel can come with overcrowded facilities, while rising land values may exclude the lower-income households expected to benefit most from convenient transport. Apartments near a station support lower car dependence only when residents can afford to live there and walking routes and public services are genuinely usable. Concentrating homes also concentrates demand for schools, public space and local services. Families may live closer to a station but still make long daily trips if local schools lack places and children must travel elsewhere for lessons. Rising land prices can also push poorer tenants away before they enjoy better connections, transferring much of the accessibility gain to households with greater purchasing power.

Planning should coordinate housing with services, green areas and affordable access. Coordinated provision needs schools, public space and affordable homes, so concentrating residents does not merely move the bottleneck from roads to other essential services. Developers and local authorities should agree school places and pedestrian access before homes are occupied, so the first residents do not spend years waiting for facilities promised in planning documents. Linking construction approvals to funded facilities and affordable homes would make development more than a concentration of buildings, ensuring that additional residents can actually use the services around them.
Overall, planning should assess travel behaviour, affordability and service capacity together, rather than treat the number of dwellings built beside a station as sufficient evidence of success.

paragraphs.quote: Planning should coordinate housing with services, green areas and affordable access.
